title: How do we expand (3j + 2k) squared both ways?
description: The square of three j plus two k is expanded with the square of a sum and again with the distributive property, then checked with j and k as one. Keeko doubts that adding the two squares is enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: the square of a sum is the two squares plus twice the first times the second. Watch for students who add only the two squares and leave out the middle term.

video_script.why: The child has expanded six x plus five, squared, in two ways. Here both terms have letters.
video_script.substitution: Put the two terms in the square of a sum, confirm with the distributive property, and check with small numbers.
video_script.anchor: three j plus two k, squared
video_script.wrong_answer: add the squares of the two terms
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the squares of the two terms and gets nine j squared plus four k squared. With j and k as one, the question gives twenty five but that answer gives only thirteen.
video_script.payoff_line: Twice the first times the second is the middle term

final_answer.spoken: nine j squared, plus twelve j k, plus four k squared

video_script.design: One idea: the square of a sum is the two squares plus twice the first times the second. Uses the method of the six x plus five video. Wrong idea: add the squares of the two terms. The cut square stays on the board through the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step one, put three j for the first term and two k for the second.
<bookmark mark='sq1'/>The square of three j is nine j squared.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice three j times two k is twelve j k.
<bookmark mark='sq2'/>The square of two k is four k squared.
That gives nine j squared, plus twelve j k, plus four k squared.

beats.colours: the two six j k pieces in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='dist'/>Step two, expand by the distributive property instead.
Three j plus two k, times three j plus two k, gives four pieces.
<bookmark mark='four'/>They are nine j squared, six j k, six j k and four k squared.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Six j k and six j k make twelve j k, so both ways agree.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Step three, check with j as one and k as one.
<bookmark mark='q'/>The question gives five squared, which is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='e'/>The answer gives nine plus twelve plus four, which is also twenty five.

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Twice the first times the second is the middle term.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The answer is nine j squared, plus twelve j k, plus four k squared.
